title: AI Agents from Scratch: Your First Autonomous Assistant
description: Curious what an AI agent actually is? This gentle introduction walks you through the agent loop of perception, planning, tool calling and observation, then has you build a small autonomous assistant that searches the web and answers questions. No prior machine learning experience is required.

title: LangGraph in Depth: State Machines for Reliable Agents
description: Model your agent as an explicit state machine instead of a tangle of if-statements. You will build cyclic LangGraph workflows with typed state, conditional edges, checkpointing and human-in-the-loop interrupts, then add durable persistence so long-running agent runs survive restarts and can be resumed or replayed.

title: Multi-Agent Collaboration Patterns
description: Move beyond single-agent scripts to teams of specialised agents. This course covers supervisor and swarm topologies, message passing protocols, task decomposition, shared scratchpad memory and conflict resolution, with hands-on labs orchestrating a researcher, a critic and a writer working toward one deliverable.

title: Tool Calling and Function Schemas for LLM Agents
description: Tools are what turn a language model into an agent. Learn to design JSON schemas that models actually call correctly, handle parallel tool calls, validate and retry malformed arguments, and wrap APIs, databases and shell commands as safe, well-documented functions with useful error messages.

title: Agent Memory Architectures: Short-Term, Episodic and Semantic
description: Agents forget unless you design memory deliberately. Compare short-term conversation buffers, episodic logs, semantic vector stores and summarisation-based compaction, then build a layered memory system with retrieval, decay and write policies so your agent recalls the right context without exhausting the token budget.

title: Planning and Reflection Loops for Autonomous Agents
description: Reliable autonomy comes from good planning. Implement ReAct, plan-and-execute and tree-of-thought strategies, add self-critique and reflection loops that let an agent detect failed steps and replan, and learn when to cap iterations to avoid runaway planning loops and spiralling token cost.

title: Build a Coding Agent: Repo-Aware Autonomous Engineering
description: Build the kind of agent that reads a repository, edits files and runs tests. You will implement repo indexing, a sandboxed shell and file-editing toolset, diff review and an iterative test-and-fix loop, then benchmark your coding agent against real GitHub issues.

title: Structured Outputs and JSON Mode for LLM Applications
description: Free-text answers break pipelines. Learn constrained decoding, JSON schema enforcement and grammar-based generation to make model output reliably parseable, then add Pydantic validation, repair passes and streaming partial objects so downstream services never choke on a stray token.

title: Embeddings Explained: From Word Vectors to Multimodal Search
description: Vectors are the foundation of modern semantic search. This course explains what embeddings are, how cosine similarity captures meaning, and how model choice, dimensionality and normalisation affect results, with notebooks comparing text, image and multilingual embedding models on real retrieval tasks.

title: LLM Evaluation: Benchmarks, LLM-as-Judge and Regression Suites
description: Shipping without evaluation is guessing. Build golden datasets, write LLM-as-judge rubrics, measure faithfulness and hallucination rates, and wire regression suites into continuous integration so every prompt or model change is scored before release. Includes practical guidance on sample sizes and confidence intervals.

title: Multimodal AI Applications: Vision, Audio and Documents
description: Text is only part of the story. Build applications that reason over images, audio and scanned documents using vision-language models, OCR fallbacks and audio transcription, then combine modalities in a single prompt pipeline for tasks like invoice extraction and video summarisation.

title: AI Agents for Business Automation
description: Automate the boring parts of your job with agents. Using low-code tooling and a handful of Python snippets you will connect an agent to email, spreadsheets and calendars, define clear tool permissions, and add approval steps so nothing important happens without a human confirming it.

title: Agent Evaluation and Observability
description: You cannot improve an agent you cannot see. Instrument trajectories with tracing, capture every tool call and intermediate thought, then score runs on task success, step efficiency and tool-selection accuracy. Build dashboards and regression suites that catch silent agent degradation before your users do.

title: Agent Safety and Guardrails
description: Autonomous systems need brakes. Design permission scopes, allow-lists and sandboxes for tools, add input and output guardrails against prompt injection and data exfiltration, and implement human-in-the-loop approval, rate limits and kill switches for high-risk actions such as payments or deletions.

title: Shipping Agents to Production
description: Take an agent from notebook to production traffic. Cover asynchronous job queues, streaming responses, durable state and checkpointing, retries and idempotency, versioned prompts, canary rollouts and on-call runbooks for the night your orchestration loop stalls halfway through a customer workflow.

title: Agent Cost and Latency Optimization
description: Agents get expensive fast. Profile token spend per step, cut redundant context with prompt caching and compaction, route easy steps to smaller models, parallelise independent tool calls and speculatively prefetch retrievals, then measure the cost and latency wins against a fixed evaluation set.

title: RAG-Powered Agents: Retrieval-Augmented Autonomy
description: Combine retrieval with autonomy. Build agents that decide when to search, rewrite their own queries, fan out across multiple knowledge sources, judge whether retrieved chunks are sufficient and loop back for more evidence before answering, with citations the user can actually verify.

title: Computer-Use and Browser Agents
description: Give an agent a keyboard and a screen. Learn screenshot-driven grounding, DOM-based browser control, action space design and verification steps that keep a computer-use agent from clicking the wrong button, plus sandboxing strategies and evaluation on real web navigation benchmarks.

title: Fine-Tuning LLMs with LoRA and QLoRA
description: When prompting is not enough, adapt the weights. Prepare instruction datasets, run parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA and QLoRA on a single GPU, tune learning rate and rank, evaluate against the base model, then merge and quantise adapters for cheap deployment.

title: Prompt Engineering for Developers
description: Prompts are code. Learn systematic techniques including role framing, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought, delimiters and explicit output contracts, then version, test and diff prompts like any other artefact. Includes a practical playbook for debugging vague, verbose or subtly wrong model responses.

title: Serving LLMs at Scale with vLLM
description: Self-hosting a model is an infrastructure problem. Learn paged attention, continuous batching, KV-cache management, quantisation and speculative decoding, then load-test a vLLM deployment behind an OpenAI-compatible gateway and tune it for throughput, tail latency and GPU utilisation.

title: Context Engineering: Caching, Compaction and Long Contexts
description: Long context windows are not free. Learn to budget tokens deliberately with prompt caching, hierarchical summarisation, context compaction and selective retrieval, and understand where models lose information in the middle so you can lay out instructions, history and evidence for maximum recall.

title: Build Your First RAG Pipeline
description: Ground a chatbot in your own documents. Starting from a folder of PDFs you will parse, chunk, embed and index the content, wire retrieval into a prompt template and add citations, ending with a working question-answering app you can point at any knowledge base.

title: Vector Databases in Practice: pgvector, Qdrant and Pinecone
description: Choose and operate the store behind your semantic search. Compare pgvector, Qdrant, Pinecone and FAISS on indexing strategy, HNSW and IVF tuning, metadata filtering and upsert throughput, then run capacity planning and benchmark recall against latency on a million-vector corpus.

title: Chunking Strategies for Retrieval Quality
description: Retrieval quality is decided long before the query arrives. Compare fixed-size, recursive, semantic and layout-aware chunking, tune overlap and window size, preserve headings and tables as metadata, and measure how each strategy shifts recall and answer faithfulness on your own evaluation set.

title: Hybrid Search: BM25 Meets Dense Vectors
description: Dense vectors miss exact identifiers and keyword search misses meaning. Build hybrid retrieval that fuses BM25 and embedding scores with reciprocal rank fusion, tune weighting per query type, and add filters and boosts so product codes, proper names and synonyms all resolve correctly.

title: Re-Ranking and Cross-Encoders for Precision Retrieval
description: Retrieve broadly, then rank precisely. This course covers cross-encoder re-rankers, ColBERT late interaction and LLM-based listwise ranking, with guidance on candidate set size, latency budgets, distillation to smaller rankers and measuring NDCG improvements over a bi-encoder baseline.

title: Knowledge Graphs and GraphRAG
description: Some questions need relationships, not passages. Extract entities and relations from unstructured text, build a property graph in Neo4j, and combine graph traversal with vector retrieval so multi-hop questions about people, products and events receive grounded, explainable answers with traceable evidence.

title: Query Understanding: Rewriting, Expansion and Intent
description: Most retrieval failures start with the query. Learn intent classification, spelling correction, query rewriting and expansion, HyDE-style hypothetical documents and multi-query fan-out, then route each intent to the right index and measure the lift on both head and long-tail traffic.

title: MLOps Foundations: Tracking, Versioning and Model Registries
description: Stop losing track of which model is in production. Learn experiment tracking, data and model versioning, reproducible training environments and model registries, then package a trained model behind a simple inference service with automated tests and a clearly documented promotion path.

title: Feature Stores and Training-Serving Skew
description: Offline accuracy means nothing if serving features differ from training ones. Build a feature store with point-in-time correct joins, share transformations between batch training and online inference, add freshness monitoring, and diagnose the skew bugs that quietly erode model performance after launch.

title: Model Monitoring and Drift Detection in Production
description: Models decay silently. Instrument production predictions, detect data and concept drift with population stability and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, set alert thresholds that do not page you nightly, and design retraining triggers plus shadow deployments that validate replacements before they take live traffic.

title: ML Pipelines on Kubernetes with Kubeflow and Argo
description: Scale training beyond a laptop. Compose containerised pipeline steps, manage GPU scheduling and spot interruptions on Kubernetes, cache expensive stages, and wire artefact lineage, hyperparameter sweeps and scheduled retraining into a system your team can operate without relying on tribal knowledge.

title: Analytics Engineering with dbt and Snowflake
description: Turn raw warehouse tables into trusted models. Learn dimensional modelling, incremental materialisations, dbt tests and documentation, and semantic layer basics, then set up continuous integration so every pull request builds and validates the transformation graph before it ever touches production dashboards.

title: Streaming Data Pipelines with Kafka and Flink
description: Batch is too slow for some problems. Design event-driven pipelines with Kafka topics and partitions, handle exactly-once semantics, watermarks and late-arriving events in Flink, and build stateful stream joins and windowed aggregations that survive consumer rebalances and full replays.

title: Airflow in Production: Reliable Batch Orchestration
description: Move past fragile cron jobs. Write idempotent, backfillable DAGs, manage dependencies and sensors, isolate tasks with Kubernetes executors, and add service level agreements, alerting and data quality checks so pipeline failures are caught and rerun before anyone downstream even notices.

title: SQL for Analytics: Window Functions and Query Tuning
description: Get genuinely fluent in the language of data. Work through joins, aggregation, window functions, common table expressions and date arithmetic on a realistic e-commerce dataset, then learn to read query plans and fix the slow queries that keep blocking your dashboards.

title: Full-Stack Next.js 15 with TypeScript
description: Build and ship a production web application with the modern React stack. Cover server components, routing and layouts, data fetching and caching, server actions, authentication and progressive enhancement, then deploy with image optimisation, edge middleware and sensible error boundaries.

title: Production APIs with FastAPI
description: Write Python APIs that hold up under load. Learn async request handling, Pydantic validation, dependency injection, SQLAlchemy sessions, background tasks and JWT authentication, then add structured logging, pagination, rate limiting and OpenAPI documentation your frontend team will actually enjoy using.

title: React Performance Optimization
description: Diagnose why your interface feels sluggish. Profile renders with React DevTools, eliminate wasted re-renders through memoisation and stable references, virtualise long lists, split bundles and tune Core Web Vitals, measuring every change instead of guessing at micro-optimisations that do nothing.

title: Server-Rendered Interactivity with HTMX
description: Not every application needs a single-page framework. Learn the hypermedia approach: swap HTML fragments over the wire with HTMX, add Alpine.js for small pieces of client state, and build a fast, accessible CRUD application backed by a plain server-rendered template stack.

title: GraphQL API Design and Federation
description: Design a graph that scales with your organisation. Cover schema design and versioning, resolvers and the N+1 problem, DataLoader batching, persisted queries and federating multiple subgraphs into one supergraph, plus authorisation and depth limiting to keep the public API safe.

title: Kubernetes for Application Developers
description: Learn just enough Kubernetes to ship confidently. Cover pods, deployments, services, ingress, config maps and secrets, resource requests and limits, health probes and rolling updates, then debug crash loops and pending pods yourself with kubectl instead of filing a platform ticket.

title: Terraform: Infrastructure as Code from Zero to Modules
description: Stop clicking through cloud consoles. Learn Terraform state, providers, variables and outputs, then refactor into reusable modules with remote state, workspaces and plan reviews in continuous integration so infrastructure changes are versioned, peer-reviewed and repeatable across every environment.

title: CI/CD Pipelines with GitHub Actions
description: Automate everything between commit and deploy. Build workflows with matrix jobs, caching and reusable composite actions, manage secrets and OIDC cloud authentication, and set up staged deployments with automatic rollback when smoke tests fail against your freshly released build.

title: Observability with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus and Grafana
description: Logs alone will not save you at three in the morning. Instrument services with OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and structured logs, propagate context across async boundaries, control cardinality and sampling cost, then build Grafana dashboards and alerts tied to real service level objectives.

title: Web Application Security: OWASP Top 10 in Practice
description: Attack your own application before somebody else does. Work hands-on through injection, broken access control, server-side request forgery, insecure deserialisation and misconfiguration in a deliberately vulnerable app, then implement the fixes and add dependency and secret scanning to your pipeline.

title: Threat Modeling for Engineering Teams
description: Security decisions are cheapest at design time. Learn to draw data flow diagrams, apply STRIDE, rank risks realistically, and run a one-hour threat modelling session your engineers will not dread, ending with tracked mitigations instead of a long document nobody reads.

title: Cloud Security and IAM Hardening on AWS
description: Most cloud breaches are identity problems. Design least-privilege IAM policies and permission boundaries, secure cross-account roles, encrypt data with KMS, detect misconfiguration through automated posture scanning, and investigate incidents using CloudTrail logs and GuardDuty findings in guided labs.

title: Prompt Injection and LLM Application Security
description: Language model features open an entirely new attack surface. Exploit and then defend against direct and indirect prompt injection, tool abuse, data exfiltration through markdown images and insecure output handling, using sandboxing, allow-lists and content provenance to contain untrusted text.

title: Design Systems in Figma: Tokens, Components and Variants
description: Build a component library your engineers can actually implement. Define colour, type and spacing tokens, create variants and auto-layout components, document usage rules, and hand off with a naming scheme that maps cleanly to code, keeping design and production genuinely in sync.

title: UX Research Fundamentals
description: Learn to find out what users truly need. Plan and run interviews and usability tests, write unbiased questions, recruit realistic participants, synthesise findings into clear themes, and present evidence that actually changes roadmap decisions rather than sitting unread in a slide deck.

title: Interaction Design for AI Products
description: AI features break familiar interface patterns. Design for uncertainty and latency with streaming responses, progress and reasoning affordances, graceful failure states, feedback capture and clear controls over automation, so users understand what the system did and can always take back the wheel.

title: Product Management for AI Features
description: Shipping AI is a product problem, not only a model problem. Learn to scope probabilistic features, define quality bars and evaluation metrics, forecast and price inference costs, run staged launches, and communicate reliability honestly to both customers and executive stakeholders.

title: System Design Interview Preparation
description: Walk into the whiteboard with a repeatable framework. Practise scoping requirements, estimating capacity and designing caches, queues, sharded databases and rate limiters, with worked solutions for feeds, chat and search systems plus guidance on communicating trade-offs under real time pressure.

title: From Engineer to Tech Lead
description: The first leadership step is the hardest one. Learn to set technical direction without writing all the code yourself, give feedback that lands, plan projects realistically, manage stakeholders and grow the people around you while protecting enough time to stay technically credible.
